question.question: What is the purpose of a 'shebang' line at the top of a Bash script?

options.text: It specifies the programming language used in the script
It sets the execution permission of the script
It tells the system which interpreter to use to run the script
It adds a comment to the script

question.explanation: The 'shebang' line, also known as the hashbang, specifies the interpreter that should be used to run the script. It is usually the first line of the script and starts with #!
